title: Criminal Law Paralegal
company: The Eventus Recruitment Group - Agency - Permanent
description:
Eventus Legal are seeking an experienced Criminal Paralegal to join a specialist criminal defence practice in Dewsbury, West Yorkshire. This full-time, permanent job is office-based and offers a competitive salary of £30,000 - £35,000 DOE plus 25 days annual leave, workplace pension scheme, paid training and professional development, paid professional memberships or accreditation renewal fees, time off in lieu of additional hours worked and reimbursement of travel expenses and free parking. You will manage a varied caseload, including Crown Court matters, with appropriate supervision from an experienced team member and opportunities to develop your expertise and progress your legal career.

Job Responsibilities

As a Criminal Paralegal, you will progress criminal defence matters from initial instruction through to conclusion, keeping clients informed throughout. Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing criminal defence files with appropriate supervision, including preparing and progressing your own Crown Court caseload
- Taking client instructions and providing clear, sensitive and professional communication throughout each matter
- Reviewing police disclosure, witness statements, exhibits and body-worn video footage
- Preparing correspondence, applications, case summaries and instructions to counsel, and supporting solicitors with hearing and trial preparation
- Liaising with police, courts, counsel, experts and other relevant agencies
- Attending police stations to assist clients where appropriately accredited
- Drafting and submitting legal aid applications
- Maintaining accurate electronic case records and meeting deadlines, court directions and case management requirements

Person Specification

You will be an experienced Criminal Paralegal with a background in criminal defence practice and a good working knowledge of criminal procedure and the criminal justice system. You should also be able to demonstrate the following:
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise competing demands under pressure
- Excellent written and verbal communication, with a confident and professional approach to clients and other professionals
- Close attention to detail and the ability to work independently while contributing positively to the team
- Flexibility to meet the demands of criminal defence work, including occasional out-of-hours requirements
- Police Station Accreditation and experience assisting clients in custody are highly desirable, particularly the ability to attend police stations independently
- Legal aid criminal defence experience and familiarity with Magistrates' Court and Crown Court proceedings are desirable
- Experience using digital case management systems and electronic bundles is desirable
- A full UK driving licence and willingness to travel to police stations and courts where required are desirable

Benefits and Rewards

This Criminal Paralegal job offers the opportunity to develop your career within a supportive and experienced criminal defence team. The successful Criminal Paralegal will also benefit from:
- Salary between £30,000 - £35,000 based on experience
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Workplace pension scheme
- Funded Police Station Accreditation
- Paid training and professional development
- Paid professional memberships or accreditation renewal fees
- Time off in lieu of additional hours worked and reimbursement of travel expenses
- Free parking
- Opportunities to develop your criminal law expertise and progress your legal career
- Full-time, permanent employment with office-based working, Monday to Friday, with flexibility and occasional out-of-hours work required

About the Law Firm

Our client is a specialist criminal defence law firm holding the Specialist Quality Mark, with a practice covering general and serious crime, fraud, road traffic offences and regulatory matters. The firm supports clients throughout the criminal justice process, providing advice and representation from initial police station attendance through to Magistrates' Court and Crown Court proceedings. You will join a busy, supportive team of experienced criminal law professionals, working on a varied caseload that offers scope to deepen your specialist knowledge and strengthen your case preparation skills. With appropriate supervision and experienced colleagues to work alongside, this opportunity will allow you to build on your existing criminal defence experience, develop your confidence in managing complex matters and progress your legal career.

title: Health and Welfare Court of Protection Paralegal
company: Simpson Millar LLP Solicitors - Agency - Permanent
description:
To provide legal and administrative support to solicitors handling Court of Protection Health and Welfare matters and ensuring clients receive high-quality, compassionate, and effective legal representation.

A Health and Welfare Court of Protection Paralegal may assist with matters involving:
- Best interests decisions
- Deprivation of Liberty (DoLS and Liberty Protection Safeguards-related matters)
- Residence and care disputes
- Contact with family members
- Medical treatment decisions
- Serious medical treatment applications
- Safeguarding concerns
- Mental capacity assessments
- Challenges to local authority or NHS decisions.

This is a rewarding area of law that combines legal analysis with direct client interaction, advocacy, and multidisciplinary working to protect the rights and welfare of vulnerable individuals.

Key Responsibilities
- Assisting solicitors with a caseload of Health and Welfare Court of Protection matters.
- Drafting court applications, witness statements, legal correspondence, attendance notes, and court bundles.
- Liaising with clients, family members, advocates, social workers, healthcare professionals, local authorities, and other agencies.
- Attending client meetings in hospitals, care homes, supported living settings, or clients' homes.
- Assisting with preparing cases for hearings and conferences with counsel.
- Managing files, maintain accurate records, and comply with regulatory and file management procedures.
- Monitoring court deadlines and ensure timely filing of documents.
- Handling new enquiries and assist with client onboarding.
- Supporting applications for legal aid where appropriate.
- Assisting with business development activities, networking, and maintaining professional relationships.
- Conducting legal research on relevant legislation and case law, including; The Mental Capacity Act 2005, The Mental Health Act 1983, The Care Act 2014 and Human rights and safeguarding law.

Key Requirements:
- Law degree, Graduate Diploma in Law (GDL), or equivalent legal qualification.
- Must have at least 12 months experience assisting with Health & welfare Court of Protection matters
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organisational and time management abilities.
- High attention to detail.
- Ability to work empathetically with vulnerable clients.
- Professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality.
- Competent in Microsoft Office and legal case management systems.
- Excellent knowledge of legal aid procedures.
- Experience attending court or client meetings.

Why Join Simpson Millar?

At Simpson Millar, you'll be part of a people-focused firm that is committed to delivering exceptional client care while supporting the development and wellbeing of its colleagues. We offer all level 2 employees:
- 26 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays and the option to purchase additional days
- We pride ourselves on offering flexibility and a healthy work-life balance, our hybrid working policy requires employees to attend the office just twice per month, however most teams get together once per week and you're more than welcome to attend as much as you like, we encourage you to find the balance that works best for you.
- Opportunities for professional development, career progression and more

Equality, Diversity & Inclusion

Simpson Millar is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone is valued, respected, and given equal opportunity to succeed. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and are dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues can be themselves, thrive, and reach their full potential. We believe that diversity of thought, experience, and perspective makes us stronger and helps us better serve our clients, colleagues, and communities
